title: 01 — Financial Domain Foundations
html:
01 — Financial Domain Foundations

The one idea: financial data is only useful when you can say which entity or instrument a number belongs to, which rulebook it was reported under, and when it was true. Identifiers answer the first question, regulators and reporting standards answer the second, and the rest of this set answers the third.

1. Why domain knowledge comes first

A data platform for financial data fails in predictable ways when the engineers do not know the domain:

  • Two rows for "Example Steel Ltd" and "EXAMPLE STEEL LIMITED" are treated as different companies.
  • A bond and the company that issued it are joined on name and silently produce the wrong exposure.
  • A restated annual figure overwrites the original, and nobody can reproduce last quarter's report.
  • A mutual fund NAV is compared across a Regular and a Direct plan, which are different prices for the same portfolio.

Every one of these is a modelling error, not a coding error. Learn the vocabulary below before designing tables.

2. Identifiers: the join keys of finance

An identifier is a code assigned by an authority so that an entity or instrument can be named without ambiguity. Names change, get abbreviated and get misspelt; identifiers (mostly) do not.

Identifier Identifies Length Issued by Shape
ISIN A security (share, bond, fund unit, government security) 12 National numbering agency (NSDL in India) IN + 9 alphanumerics + 1 check digit
CIN A company registered in India 21 Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) Listing flag, industry, state, year, ownership type, registration number
PAN A taxpayer (person, company, firm, trust …) 10 Income Tax Department AAAAA9999A
LEI A legal entity taking part in financial transactions, globally 20 A Local Operating Unit accredited by GLEIF 18 alphanumerics + 2 check digits
AMFI scheme code A mutual fund scheme plan/option 5–6 digits Association of Mutual Funds in India Numeric

2.1 ISIN in detail

I N E 0 0 2 A 0 1 0 1 8
└┬┘ └───────┬───────┘ └ check digit
 │        NSIN (9 chars: issuer + security)
 country code (ISO 3166)
  • Indian prefixes you will see: INE… for securities of companies, INF… for mutual fund units, IN0…/IN1…-style codes for government securities and state development loans.
  • The last character is a check digit: letters are converted to numbers (A=10 … Z=35), then a Luhn-style algorithm runs over the digits. Validate it at ingestion — a single wrong character is the most common error in hand-typed data.
  • One company has many ISINs (equity, each bond series, each fund plan). An ISIN identifies an instrument, not an entity.
def isin_is_valid(isin: str) -> bool:
    if len(isin) != 12 or not isin[:2].isalpha() or not isin[-1].isdigit():
        return False
    digits = "".join(str(int(c, 36)) for c in isin[:-1].upper())   # 'A' -> '10'
    total = 0
    # Luhn: double every second digit counting from the right of the payload
    for i, d in enumerate(reversed(digits)):
        n = int(d)
        if i % 2 == 0:
            n *= 2
            n = n - 9 if n > 9 else n
        total += n
    return (10 - total % 10) % 10 == int(isin[-1])

2.2 CIN in detail

A CIN such as L17110MH1990PLC012345 decodes as:

Part Example Meaning
1 char L L = listed, U = unlisted
5 digits 17110 Industry code (National Industrial Classification)
2 letters MH State of registration
4 digits 1990 Year of incorporation
3 letters PLC Ownership: PLC public, PTC private, GOI government, FLC/FTC foreign subsidiary …
6 digits 012345 Registration number at the Registrar of Companies

Useful consequence: the CIN changes when a company goes from unlisted to listed (U → L). Treat a CIN as an attribute with history, not as an eternal primary key.

2.3 PAN in detail

AAACE1234F: five letters, four digits, one check letter. The fourth letter is the holder type (P individual, C company, H Hindu Undivided Family, F firm, T trust, A association of persons, G government …). The fifth letter is the first letter of the holder's name (or surname for individuals).

A PAN is personal data when it belongs to an individual. Mask it in logs and lower environments, and never put it in a URL.

2.4 LEI in detail

ISO 17442. Characters 1–4 identify the issuing operating unit, 5–18 identify the entity, 19–20 are check digits computed with ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 (the same family as IBAN). GLEIF publishes the full LEI database openly, including parent relationships ("who owns whom"), which makes it a free source for corporate group structures.

def lei_is_valid(lei: str) -> bool:
    if len(lei) != 20 or not lei.isalnum():
        return False
    as_digits = "".join(str(int(c, 36)) for c in lei.upper())
    return int(as_digits) % 97 == 1

2.5 Instrument vs entity — the model that falls out

---
title: Entities, instruments and identifiers
---
erDiagram
    LEGAL_ENTITY ||--o{ INSTRUMENT : issues
    LEGAL_ENTITY ||--o{ ENTITY_IDENTIFIER : "known as"
    INSTRUMENT ||--o{ INSTRUMENT_IDENTIFIER : "known as"
    LEGAL_ENTITY }o--o| LEGAL_ENTITY : "parent of"
    INSTRUMENT ||--o{ PRICE_OR_NAV : "valued by"
    LEGAL_ENTITY ||--o{ FINANCIAL_REPORT : files
  • ENTITY_IDENTIFIER holds CIN, PAN, LEI rows (type, value, valid period).
  • INSTRUMENT_IDENTIFIER holds ISIN, exchange symbol, AMFI code.
  • Keep your own surrogate ID for each entity and instrument ("canonical ID"). External identifiers are attributes that point at it. Chapter 10 shows how records without clean identifiers get matched to that canonical ID.

3. Regulators and what they publish

Body Regulates Data you will meet
SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) Capital markets: exchanges, listed companies, mutual funds, brokers, rating agencies Listing disclosures, shareholding patterns, BRSR, mutual fund categorisation rules, rating actions
RBI (Reserve Bank of India) Banks, NBFCs, payment systems, monetary policy Asset classification (NPA), provisioning, credit reporting, early-warning frameworks
MCA (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) Company law CIN registry, director identification numbers (DIN), annual filings
AMFI Industry body for mutual funds Scheme master, daily NAV file, monthly AUM
IRDAI, PFRDA Insurance, pensions Less common in these notes

3.1 BRSR — sustainability reporting

The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report is SEBI's ESG disclosure format for the largest listed companies by market capitalisation. It is structured around nine principles (ethics, product responsibility, employee well-being, stakeholders, human rights, environment, policy advocacy, inclusive growth, customer value). A subset of key indicators — BRSR Core — carries reasonable-assurance requirements.

Why it matters to a data engineer: BRSR arrives as PDF and XBRL, values are restated, and units vary (tonnes vs kilotonnes, kWh vs GJ). It is a textbook case for document extraction, unit normalisation and bitemporal storage.

3.2 Credit risk vocabulary (banking side)

  • NPA (Non-Performing Asset): a loan where interest or principal is overdue for more than 90 days. Sub-classified by age: substandard (NPA up to 12 months), doubtful, loss.

  • SMA (Special Mention Account): the early-warning buckets before NPA — SMA-0 (1–30 days overdue), SMA-1 (31–60), SMA-2 (61–90).

  • ECL (Expected Credit Loss) under Ind AS 109 (India's version of IFRS 9): provisions are booked for losses expected, not only incurred.

    ECL = PD × LGD × EAD   (discounted to present value)

PD  = probability of default over the horizon
LGD = loss given default (share of exposure not recovered)
EAD = exposure at default

    Three stages decide the horizon:

    Stage Condition ECL horizon
    1 Performing, no significant increase in credit risk 12 months
    2 Significant increase in credit risk since origination Lifetime
    3 Credit-impaired (in default) Lifetime, interest on net carrying amount

  • Internal Rating System: a lender's own scale mapping borrowers to PD bands. External ratings (AAA, AA+ …) from rating agencies feed into it.

  • Early Warning System (EWS): a set of signals — delayed filings, auditor resignation, pledged promoter shares, rating downgrades, negative news — that flag distress before default. Chapter 11 shows how text signals are extracted from filings.

3.3 Mutual fund vocabulary

Term Meaning
AMC Asset Management Company — runs the funds
Scheme A fund with one portfolio and one objective
Plan Direct (no distributor commission, lower expense ratio) or Regular
Option Growth (returns stay in NAV) or IDCW (income distributed)
NAV Net Asset Value per unit = (assets − liabilities) ÷ units outstanding, published daily
AUM Assets under management
TER Total expense ratio

Each plan × option combination has its own NAV, ISIN and AMFI code, even though the portfolio is the same.

4. Time in financial data

Three different dates appear on almost every financial fact:

Date Example Name used later
The period the number describes Revenue for FY 2025-26 Valid time (valid_from / valid_to)
The date it was published Annual report filed on 2026-08-14 Knowledge or transaction time (known_from)
The date you loaded it Pipeline ran on 2026-08-15 Ingestion time

Numbers get restated: a company revises last year's revenue in this year's report, a rating agency withdraws a rating, AMFI corrects a NAV. If your tables keep only "the latest value", you can no longer answer "what did we believe on 30 June?" — which is exactly what an auditor or a model validator asks. Chapter 09 solves this.

5. Core developer baseline

The rest of this set assumes:

  • Python 3.11+ — virtual environments (uv venv or python -m venv), type hints, async/await basics.
  • SQL — CTEs, window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LAG, LEAD), and temporal joins (joining a fact to the dimension row valid at that date).
  • Docker Compose — to run object storage, PostgreSQL, Redis and a vector database locally.

A temporal join, since it appears everywhere later:

-- Attach the rating that was in force on each NAV date
SELECT n.isin, n.nav_date, n.nav, r.rating
FROM nav n
LEFT JOIN issuer_rating r
  ON  r.issuer_id = n.issuer_id
  AND n.nav_date >= r.valid_from
  AND n.nav_date <  r.valid_to;      -- half-open interval: [from, to)

Always use half-open intervals [from, to) with an open end represented as 9999-12-31 (or NULL handled explicitly). They tile time with no gaps and no overlaps.

6. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why should a table of companies not use ISIN as its primary key?
  2. A CIN starts with U in 2019 and L in 2024. What happened, and how should your table represent it?
  3. Compute by hand whether an ECL stage-2 loan has a 12-month or lifetime horizon, and why that matters for provisioning volatility.
  4. Two NAVs for the "same" fund on the same day differ by 0.8%. Name two legitimate reasons.
  5. Write the SQL to find, for each ISIN, the NAV on the last business day of each month.

7. Review checklist

  • Every identifier has a validator (length, alphabet, check digit) at ingestion.
  • Entities and instruments are separate tables, linked by an issuer relationship.
  • External identifiers are stored with their own validity periods.
  • PAN and other personal identifiers are masked outside production.
  • Every fact records the period it describes and when it was published.
